topology: Inside VLAN1 access LAN on SW1: PC1 192.168.10.10/24, PC2 .20, WEB1 .50, gateway R1 Gi0/0 192.168.10.1. R1 Gi0/1 203.0.113.1/24 faces ISP1 Gi0/0 .2; ISP1 Gi0/1 198.51.100.1/24 faces SRV1 .10 with gateway .1. Static WEB1 global203.0.113.10, one-address PUBLIC pool203.0.113.20/24, final interface PAT203.0.113.1. ISP1 has no private-LAN return route. Host/switch addressing and both HTTP pages are prepared; R1 NAT and default route are absent from practice.
verificationNotes: Adds first IP Services subsection entry under CCNP ENCOR without changing CCNA Static NAT or PAT. The new subsection has an accessible singular1-lab badge; all three prior ENCOR subsection counts remain3/6/9.

Practice starts0/18. One actual R1 baseline command set configures NAT roles, default route, exact /24 standard classifier, static server publication, one-address pool and basic dynamic rule, earning six live goals. PC1 actual translated ping earns allocation; PC2 actual failed allocation with correlated returned ICMP error earns exhaustion; clear removes dynamic state while preserving the static mapping; PC2 then really reuses the released public address.

Dynamic failure proof requires live PC1 ownership and correlated successful PC1 traffic, real PC2 source send and R1 ingress receipt, actual NAT-pool-exhaustion drop and a parent-correlated quoted ICMP error at PC2. Failed preconfiguration, missing routing, shutdown and NAT-direction faults do not substitute for exhaustion. Per-attempt configuration epochs reject stale probes.

Actual clear-and-replace commands remove the basic pool rule and install outside-interface overload. Two live ICMP bindings share203.0.113.1 with unique translated identifiers and matching replies. Separate complete TCP/HTTP200 deliveries are required for both inside clients. An outside ping and actual outside browser HTTP200 verify inbound destination translation and the static server's reverse source translation.

Static WEB1 precedence over the matching /24 classifier is tested even with the basic pool occupied. Dynamic NAT keeps one address binding per inside host, with separate ICMP/TCP child entries that preserve ports/identifiers; PAT distinguishes clients with translated identifiers/ports. In-use rule/pool edits reject before mutation until clearing state.

Completed reference contains final saved static+PAT configuration, retained previously exercised PUBLIC definition and empty runtime; initially8/18 live tasks with no invented allocations, failures, pings or HTTP. Dedicated reverse-transition commands revisit dynamic stages without reapplying the source ACL, then final PAT and traffic complete18.

Tests cover routing/role faults, private-return-route shortcuts, classifier exclusion, stale and tampered packet evidence, missing/404 HTTP service, per-client application evidence, healthy startup equality, extra-rule rejection, IOS reload, portable reopening, contextual question-mark/Tab help and every published verification command. Existing TCP/NAT/packet engine unchanged.

Packet achievements persist across offline reopen, while dynamic translation/flow state rebuilds from actual new traffic and current configuration/routing/save checks remain live. Existing terminal layout/colors/fonts and general UI preserved.

Scope is IOS IPv4 inside-source static NAT, basic pool dynamic NAT and interface PAT, not outside-source NAT, hairpin, NAT64, ALG behavior or complete platform parity. Checked against Cisco primary documentation and existing CML NAT replay contracts in the full suite; no new live CML capture is claimed.
